title: Background-thread dataloader prefetch
description: Wrapped prepare.py's make_dataloader in a background prefetch thread (clone the reused buffers, worker waits on its own copy). val_bpb 0.997854, 406.1M tokens, MFU 32.6% - no improvement; an earlier attempt in the same slot that also replaced best-fit packing with contiguous stream packing was much worse (1.004606) despite 454M tokens.
reflection: Two negatives with one large positive finding. (1) I measured prepare.py's loader off-GPU at 68.6ms median / 77ms mean per 64x2048 batch, almost the whole 80ms step, and concluded it was stalling the GPU. It is not: CUDA async already hides it, because loss.backward() returns immediately and the loader's Python runs while the GPU drains. My prefetch thread made throughput WORSE (406.1M tokens, 32.6% MFU, vs 416-422M and 33.4-33.9% for the identical inline code in round 0) - the per-batch stream sync needed to keep the loader's reused pinned buffer safe, plus clone and GIL contention, costs more than the stall it removes. The ~80ms step is real GPU compute, so MFU 33-39% is genuine kernel inefficiency, not a data stall; nobody should spend another run chasing dataloader stalls. (2) The first attempt changed packing as well as threading and isolated the cell's biggest effect so far: contiguous-stream packing (documents concatenated and sliced, rows starting mid-document) cost about +0.012 bpb - 1.0046 with MORE tokens (454.2M) than any round-0 run. That is ten times larger than anything on the batch-size axis (0.0003-0.0012) and well outside the 0.0019 replication noise. BOS-aligned, non-fragmenting best-fit packing is worth ~0.012 bpb and must not be replaced. The useful corollary for later rounds: if fragmenting documents costs 0.012, then packing/masking is the most sensitive axis anyone has found, and changes in the other direction - document-boundary-aware attention so rows cannot attend across packed documents - are where I would look next.
